question: Does 16-record submission reduce the idle driver interval more than the retained 64-record candidate, while preserving exact all66 and the original single-command controls?

parameters.regression: 218 tests / 25 explicit opt-in skips / 0 failures; release build
parameters.cache_state: same prepared archive; source pages unspecified; no reloading between arms
parameters.one_factor: records per submitted command: single control / 16 / single return control; all commands complete before publication, same queue, kernel, masks, exact arithmetic and buffers
parameters.environment: QUANTEM_TANS_SPLIT_COMMANDS=1; QUANTEM_TANS_RECORDS_PER_COMMAND=16; QUANTEM_TANS_HOLD_IDLE_SECONDS=4; QUANTEM_TANS_HOLD_CYCLES=2; full66 fixture and native-mask replay paths
parameters.matrix: 9 matched real-native masks, 2 cycles per arm, A/B/A = 54 queries; frozen independent Linux BF/ADF/ABF image comparisons plus full66 output hashes and 198 native probes per mask
parameters.decision: Require both controls beaten without altered counts/memory/loading; then separate warm, safety and native qualification. No direct 16-versus64 causal claim from different processes.
parameters.timing: Full query wall is primary. GPU first-to-last span includes scheduling; not shader-active or native FPS. Per-command driver metric refers only to last command.
parameters.memory: No new resident/index/scratch scientific data; bounded additional command objects only. Record process samples, system compressor/swap and Metal currentAllocatedSize. No fake keepalive or power change.
parameters.result: 54/54 full66 queries exact. Idle case2 A1/B/A2 p50 671.008/443.304/667.560ms; case7 873.801/443.162/873.613ms. All9 case medians beat both single-command controls, but 16 does not establish superiority over64 across separate runs. Extra encode span approximately40-50ms versus earlier64 approximately10ms. No warm/native/default adoption. No120FPS claim.
